trigger: forward_gateway_pending()'s detached thread concurrently calling analytics_store_.lock() while ServerImpl::stop() concurrently writes to the same weak_ptr instance via set_analytics_store({})
policy_floor: ownership/lifetime defect (data race, TSan-confirmed on a minimal reproducer of this exact shape) per cpp-safety blocking contract
summary: The 65c9fab4d shared_ptr/weak_ptr conversion (itself fixing FJARVIS-UAF) retained the raw-pointer siblings' unwire-then-reset teardown habit -- server.cpp's stop() called set_analytics_store({}) to clear the weak_ptr members, an unsynchronized write racing the detached thread's concurrent .lock() reads on the SAME weak_ptr instance. A genuine data race, narrower in practical impact than the original raw-pointer UAF (a torn weak_ptr read most likely yields an empty/failing lock(), not a wild dereference) but zero test coverage existed for this concurrent path. Root cause: a weak_ptr does not need explicit clearing the way a raw pointer does -- the owning shared_ptr's own reset() already atomically expires the shared control block for every locker.
adjudication_rationale: Fix: deleted both set_analytics_store({}) calls from stop(). Verified (cpp-safety re-review, pass 6): the two wiring calls at ServerImpl construction (server.cpp:4562,4575) are now the weak_ptr members' ONLY writes, ever -- confirmed no std::thread is spawned anywhere between ServerImpl's constructor start and those two calls completing, so forward_gateway_pending() (the sole spawner of the detached reader thread) structurally cannot race them. Write-once-before-concurrency, race-free by construction, not by convention. Repo-wide grep confirmed no other set_analytics_store call site exists (tests included).

provenance: introduced (by 65c9fab4d leaving a now-stale enumeration in an adjacent, unmodified comment block)
summary: The pre-existing #3279 SCOPE NOTE (2026-08-19) enumerated analytics_store_ alongside response_store_/notification_store_ as reached via 'their own plain (non-atomic) pointers' -- true when written, false as of 65c9fab4d's weak_ptr conversion. Standing rule 3: a comment that contradicts the code is a truth finding any agent may raise, wording-only is capped at NICE, but a truth contradiction is native severity.

ADR-0049's established 'Correction (...)' block convention had no entry for this round's ownership-model change (SEC-5 -> FJARVIS-UAF -> shared_ptr/weak_ptr fix) despite it being the store's most consequential lifecycle finding to date. Also: the ~15-call-site idiom was quoted as a uniform `if (analytics_store_) { ... }` in two places, no longer accurate for the 15 sites now using weak_ptr::lock(). New changelog.d fragment: not required (verified empirically -- ADR-0049 absent from origin/dev, merge-base predates its introduction -- same reasoning as the earlier an-compliance-1 adjudication).

Three comments (analytics_event_store.cpp emit(), analytics_event_store.hpp shutting_down_ member, server.cpp stop()) claimed shutting_down_ makes the pool_-access window closed absolutely ('no wider than reading a nullptr'). It's a latch, not a rundown guard -- a caller already past the check when pg_pool_.reset() runs isn't blocked. Reworded to state the real guarantee: bounded by the multi-second span between stop_drain() and pg_pool_.reset(), small in practice, not zero by construction. Idiom/convention review otherwise clean: all 15 call sites correctly converted, headers/includes correct, no BLOCKING/SHOULD on naming, RAII, or test conventions.

Verdict: race genuinely closed. Traced all writes to both weak_ptr members repo-wide (exactly 2, both at ServerImpl construction, before any thread exists); confirmed weak_ptr::lock() is a const member function safe for concurrent multi-reader access per the standard's control-block thread-safety guarantee; confirmed shared_ptr::reset() correctly defers destruction when a detached thread holds a locked copy. Two residuals surfaced, both pre-existing and already documented as accepted exceptions, not new: the shutting_down_ TOCTOU (CPP-EXPERT-COMMENT-OVERCLAIM's subject) and the #3279 detached-thread class itself. Suggested follow-up (not blocking): a TSan regression test pinning the write-once-before-concurrency property, since the round's TSan evidence is an attributed reproducer, not a committed test.
